personnel_scale_guard: Kwajalein/Roi-Namur total remains within the previously closed roughly 8,200-8,900 work band; no hidden extra regiment is spawned.
doctrine_loaded: Tarawa-derived lagoon-side fire planning and anti-LVT choke-point preparation where geography permits
alternate command/succession and local reserve plans
distributed ammunition/water/telephone and smaller protected magazines
dummy positions and protected crew shelters
no post-Kwajalein deep-cave defense doctrine retrojected

survival_state.interpretation: The defense is materially more coherent than a fully surprised historical-equivalent garrison, but repeated US fire has heavily reduced exposed guns, observation and island-wide coordination.

vehicle_armor_trace.Japan_Kwajalein: No traced Japanese combat tank platoon credited.
vehicle_armor_trace.Japan_Roi: No traced Japanese combat tank platoon credited.

Japan_Namur.role: mobile/static machine-gun firepoint only; no meaningful anti-M4 capability

vehicle_armor_trace.Japanese_vehicle_branch_effect: Better running-gear/maintenance/recovery is loaded for actual traced vehicles and prime movers, but tiny bombarded islands cap reappearance; no generic tank-count bonus is applied.
vehicle_armor_trace.US_vehicle_note: US LVT/LVT(A), medium and light tank packages retain Tarawa-derived redundancy and traffic-control planning. The 5-Feb LST mission-kill reduces margin but does not delete a named tank company without cargo trace.

ground_assessment: Defense can impose higher first-day friction through prepared lagoon-side fires, surviving mortars, local reserves and remanning after bombardment. It lacks depth, armor and resupply to stop a sustained division-scale landing once US tanks/engineers/artillery are ashore.
